descriptionChirho: To hunt wild animals for food or sport, used literally of pursuing game (Gen 27:5 Esau hunting venison; Job 38:39 hunting prey for the lioness).
To pursue, stalk, or persecute a person as if hunting prey, used figuratively of enemies tracking down the righteous or God pursuing someone (Job 10:16; Lam 4:18; Ps 140:12).
To trap or ensnare persons, especially their souls, with an intensive connotation of deceptive entrapment; used of false prophetesses in Ezekiel 13 who ensnare souls through divination.
